desc: Billed as the first gathering of its kind bringing lawmakers, UAP researchers and whistleblowers together in Washington, sponsored by the Disclosure Foundation and held on 25 June 2026. Its concrete output was Eric Burlison's announcement that MIT Lincoln Laboratory had agreed to make available a 1952 recording relating to the Washington, D.C. sightings. Disclosure Foundation executive director Jordan Flowers used the occasion to describe the change in method: 'The gloves are coming off, in terms of pushing for transparency, and knowing where these things are and pulling them out of the right structures.' The forum matters to this domain because it marks the point at which the House effort stopped being organised around hearings - which require witnesses willing to be exposed - and started being organised around records demands aimed at named institutions, which do not.
